clue.text: Supply of ammo that could be monthly

blocks.note: first meaning: the chamber or store holding cartridges for a gun
second meaning: a periodical publication, many of which come out each month

explanation.surface: A soldier's ammunition delivery that arrives once a month.
explanation.walkthrough: The two halves read as one description of ammunition, but the second is a separate sense: a periodical such as a monthly.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a cartridge holder or arms store and a periodical publication issued at regular intervals.

clue.text: Jam from mother and boy: something said to make you smile

blocks.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse
a son is a male child

blocks.clueFragment: something said to make you smile
blocks.note: the word photographers ask you to say so your mouth forms a smile

explanation.surface: A family photo session where mother and son make jam and say something for the camera.
explanation.walkthrough: Damson cheese is a thick, firm preserve made from damson plums, a traditional British conserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Damson cheese is a stiff fruit preserve, so it is a kind of jam spread or conserve made from plums.

clue.text: Daughter involved in Me Too briefly getting awards

indicators.note: something said briefly is cut short, so the word for too loses its last letter
being involved in something puts you inside it, so the daughter's letter goes within the other pieces

blocks.note: taken as written
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
also means too; cut short it loses its final O

explanation.surface: A daughter caught up in the Me Too movement ends up receiving honours.
explanation.walkthrough: Me Too reads as the name of the campaign, but the two words work separately, and the daughter sits between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Medals are metal discs given as honours for achievement or bravery, so they are awards.

clue.text: Loincloths do this after being adjusted

indicators.note: adjusted letters have been altered and moved about, so the two short words are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to put on loincloths once they have been altered to fit.
explanation.definitionFit: A dhoti is the length of cloth wrapped around the waist and legs worn by men in India, a form of loincloth.

clue.text: Yours truly on steamship causing chaos

blocks.note: yours truly is a jokey way of saying myself
SS is the prefix for a steamship

explanation.surface: The writer boards a steamer and stirs up trouble on the voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: A mess is a state of disorder and confusion, which is what chaos means.

clue.text: Harm caused by eg a crazy reversal

indicators.note: the word itself tells us to turn the phrase round and read it from the end

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
mad means crazy

explanation.surface: Damage blamed on, for example, a sudden mad change of direction.
explanation.walkthrough: EG A MAD read backwards spells DAMAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Damage is injury or loss inflicted on something, the same meaning as the noun or verb harm.

clue.text: Poor journalist, meeting editor, coughed uncomfortably?

blocks.note: a hack is a writer of dull, low-grade journalism
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A second-rate reporter meets the editor and splutters nervously.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is a looser sense: a hacking cough is a dry, harsh one.
explanation.definitionFit: To hack is to give a dry rasping cough, so someone who hacked coughed in a harsh, painful way.

clue.text: Opposing allegation in a court Clem rubbished

indicators.note: something rubbished is torn apart and treated as junk, so these letters are broken up and remade

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A legal opponent's assertion that a man called Clem dismissed in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterclaim is a claim made against someone who has already brought a claim, so it is an allegation in opposition.

clue.text: Size and state of Boston

blocks.note: first meaning: bulk or quantity of matter
second meaning: the abbreviation for the US state whose capital is Boston

explanation.surface: Remarking on the scale and condition of an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like condition, but it is the US state of Massachusetts, abbreviated Mass.
explanation.definitionFit: Mass means bulk or magnitude, and it is the short form of Massachusetts, where Boston is the capital.

clue.text: Muralist's unusual concern for others

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the painter's word is put into an odd new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wall painter shows rare kindness towards other people.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s stands for 'is': the painter's word is unusual, that is, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Altruism is selfless regard for the welfare of other people, putting their interests before your own.

clue.text: One entering party with New York's American wine god!

indicators.note: something entering goes inside, so the numeral is placed within the word for a party

blocks.note: a do is a party or celebration
I is the Roman numeral one
NY is the abbreviation for New York, with the S of the possessive
US is short for American, as in United States

explanation.surface: A guest arrives at a New York party bearing American wine and declares it divine.
explanation.definitionFit: Dionysus is the Greek deity of wine, revelry and festivity, known to the Romans as Bacchus.

clue.text: Mysterious thing appearing regularly in outflow

indicators.note: showing up regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the next word is taken

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A strange object keeps turning up in a stream of water pouring out.
explanation.definitionFit: An unidentified flying object is an unexplained sighting in the sky, an enigmatic thing nobody can account for.

clue.text: Even ebb and flow in sound

indicators.note: in sound means as it is heard spoken, so we want a word pronounced like the sea's movement

blocks.note: the tide is the regular ebb and flow of the sea

explanation.surface: A calm sea whose rise and fall makes a steady sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even' looks like an adjective describing the water; it means level in a contest, as in a tied score.
explanation.definitionFit: Two sides that are tied have equal scores, so the game is even or level.

clue.text: Learned European eccentric cut dead

indicators.note: eccentric means odd and off-centre, so the following words are jumbled into a strange order

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A scholarly but oddball European snubs someone completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' seems to describe the European, but it acts on the words after it. To cut dead is to ignore someone pointedly.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned here is the adjective meaning well schooled and knowledgeable, the same sense as educated.

clue.text: Some game show network

indicators.note: some means a part of, so the letters lie within the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A quiz programme broadcast on a television channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Network' looks like a broadcaster in this surface; it means an open web of threads.
explanation.definitionFit: A mesh is an interlaced structure of wires or threads, which is a network in its physical sense.

clue.text: Our mail's redirected to a place in the sun

indicators.note: post that is redirected is sent along a new route, so these letters are sent into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Our post is forwarded to a sunny holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A place in the sun' is an idiom for a comfortable position, but here it is read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A solarium is a room or terrace built to admit sunlight for sunbathing, literally a spot in the sunshine.

clue.text: Division in mollusc: his membrane

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of the first word, the second, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A biology note about a split in a shellfish's tissue.
explanation.definitionFit: A schism is a split or rift between groups, especially within a church, so it is a division.

clue.text: Problem walking I had, that's clear

blocks.note: a limp is an uneven, impaired gait
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone admits plainly that they had trouble walking.
explanation.definitionFit: Limpid describes water or prose that is transparent and lucid, so clear in either sense.

clue.text: Attorney with information to act badly somewhere in Greater London

blocks.note: DA is a district attorney, the US public prosecutor
gen is British slang for information
to ham is to overact

explanation.surface: A lawyer armed with facts puts on a poor performance in a London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: Dagenham is a town in east London, long known for its Ford car plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Dagenham is a district in the borough of Barking and Dagenham, part of the Greater London area.

clue.text: Be featured in short commercial lying down?

indicators.note: to be featured in something is to appear within it, so the verb goes inside

blocks.note: an ad is a short form of advertisement
taken as written

explanation.surface: Appearing in a brief television advert while reclining.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: abed means in bed, where one is usually lying down.
explanation.definitionFit: Abed is an old word meaning in bed, the place one rests horizontally, so it suggests reclining.

clue.text: Burden is nothing when carried by boy

blocks.note: a lad is a boy
O is the shape of zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A weight is no bother when a boy carries it.
explanation.definitionFit: A load is a heavy weight to be carried, and figuratively a responsibility, both senses of burden.

clue.text: Riotous scenes appear to revolve around the Spanish

around means surrounding, so the Spanish article is placed within

blocks.note: to seem is to appear
el is the Spanish for the

explanation.definitionFit: A melee is a confused hand-to-hand fight or scuffle in a crowd, a disorderly scene.

clue.text: I remain with Mike in the same place

blocks.note: taken as written
to bide is to stay or wait
Mike is the radio alphabet word for M

explanation.surface: Someone says they will stay put with a friend called Mike.
explanation.walkthrough: Ibidem is the Latin footnote term, usually shortened to ibid.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibidem is Latin used in citations to refer back to the source just cited, meaning from the same location.
